items.title: Turkey confirms second ship crosses Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Three ships appear to enter Hormuz by new route along Oman coast

items.description:
A second Turkish-flagged ship has crossed the Strait of Hormuz, Turkey's Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloğlu confirmed on Saturday, even as a fleet of Omani tankers charted a new route through the contested waterway that bypasses Iran's controlled corridor entirely.[1][2]

The developments mark a cautious expansion of traffic through the strait, which has seen a roughly 95 percent drop in daily vessel movements since the U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the conflict on February 28. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps imposed a selective blockade around March 14, routing permitted ships through a checkpoint between the Iranian islands of Larak and Qeshm.[3][4][5]

items.title: Polymarket bets on $120 oil jump after Iran strikes Gulf

featured_image.name: WTI crude oil price flips Brent as Polymarket traders sees ...

items.description:
Oil prices surged to their highest levels since 2022 this week after Iran launched a fresh wave of strikes on Gulf energy infrastructure, sending prediction market bettors scrambling to price in the possibility of even steeper gains. On Polymarket, the implied probability that WTI crude will touch $120 per barrel at some point in April has climbed to 77%, according to the platform's live market data, up from 65% just days earlier.[1][2]

The repricing followed a dramatic escalation on Friday, April 3, when Iranian drones struck Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi oil refinery — which has a capacity of 346,000 barrels per day — setting off fires across the facility. Kuwait also reported an Iranian attack that caused material damage to a power and water desalination plant. Separately, Abu Dhabi suspended operations at its largest natural gas processing facility after debris from a projectile interception sparked a fire, and Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted several drones.[3][4][5]

items.title: Meta halts work with AI startup Mercor after data breach

items.description: Meta has suspended all collaboration with AI training startup Mercor while investigating a data breach that may have exposed sensitive AI industry information, according to a report from Wired on Friday and confirmed by a person familiar with the matter to Business Insider. The pause has left thousands of contractors unable to log hours on Meta-related AI training projects.[1][2][3]
